In detail · 19 nights

South Korea, properly

A clockwise loop: down the west side, out to the islands, up the east coast. Seoul stays short on purpose — the rest is what you have not seen.

19nights
8stops
±€950return flight
±€2,300all in, per person
01

Seoul

3 nights

Kept deliberately short — you have been, and the rest of this route is the point.

  • Bukchon and Ikseon-dong for the hanok lanes that survived the rebuild
  • Gwangjang market for bindaetteok and raw beef, standing up, elbow to elbow
  • One palace only — Changdeokgung, for the Secret Garden

Start · Incheon ICN Land at Incheon, AREX to Seoul Station in 43 min.

02

Asan

1 night

The stop nobody plans, which is exactly why it works. Hot springs and a 500-year-old village an hour from the capital.

  • Oeam Folk Village — thatched houses and stone walls still lived in, not staged
  • Onyang hot springs, in use since the Joseon kings came here to bathe
  • Hyeonchungsa, the shrine to Admiral Yi Sun-sin, set in pine forest

KTX 35 min · Cheonan-Asan Straight down the Gyeongbu KTX line — barely leaves the platform before it arrives.

03

Jeonju

2 nights

Where Korean food is from. The hanok village is touristed, but the eating is the real reason.

  • Bibimbap where it was invented — Hanguk-jip or Gajok Hoegwan
  • Makgeolli alleys: order a kettle, the side dishes arrive unasked and keep coming
  • Jeonju Hanok Village at 7am, before the rental-hanbok crowds

±1.5 h by rail Regional train or bus south-west into Jeolla.

04

Cheongsando

2 nights

A slow island off the south coast — Asia's first Cittaslow. Stone-walled terraced fields dropping to the sea, and almost no one.

  • Slow Walking Trail 11 — the one from the film Seopyeonje, along the ridge
  • Gudeuljangnon terraced paddies, an irrigation system found nowhere else
  • Stay in a minbak and eat whatever the boat brought in

Bus to Wando + 50 min ferry This is the leg that makes the trip unusual. Bus to Wando, ferry across.

05

Jeju

4 nights

Volcanic, subtropical, and much wilder than the honeymoon reputation suggests once you leave the resort strip.

  • Hallasan — Gwaneumsa route up, Seongpanak down, a full day
  • Seongsan Ilchulbong at sunrise, then Udo island by ferry
  • One or two Olle trail sections along the south coast
  • Haenyeo divers at Hado or Jongdal, working the water in their seventies

Ferry from Wando ~2.5 h, or fly Ferry from Wando if you want the sea approach; flights are cheap and 40 minutes.

06

Busan

3 nights

Second city, and the one people wish they had given more time. Mountains, beaches and fish markets stacked on top of each other.

  • Gamcheon Culture Village early, before the tour buses
  • Jagalchi fish market — pick it downstairs, eat it upstairs
  • Haedong Yonggungsa, a temple built onto the rocks over the sea
  • An evening at Gwangalli with the bridge lit

Flight ~1 h Short hop from Jeju, or the overnight ferry if you would rather.

07

Gyeongju

2 nights

The Silla capital for a thousand years. An entire city that is essentially an open-air museum, with burial mounds in the middle of roundabouts.

  • Bulguksa and Seokguram at opening time
  • Daereungwon tumuli park, and Cheomseongdae observatory at dusk
  • Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond after dark, when it is lit and reflected

±1 h Commuter distance from Busan — train or bus.

08

Gangneung

2 nights

The east coast, and the last stop before the run home. Cold clear sea, pine forest, and Korea's coffee obsession in concentrated form.

  • Anmok Coffee Street — roasters on the sand, which is where the obsession started
  • Gyeongpo beach and lake, and Ojukheon if the weather turns
  • Sundubu-jjigae at Chodang tofu village, made with seawater

±3.5 h across the peninsula The cross-country leg. Slow, but the alternative is backtracking through Seoul.

What it costs

Return flight AMS–ICN±€950
Beds · 19 nights±€620
Food±€420
Trains, buses, ferries±€230
Entries & extras±€120
Per person±€2,340

Mid-range: guesthouses and business hotels, eating where locals eat, no internal flights except Jeju–Busan.

Worth knowing

  • Visa — none needed for a Dutch passport up to 90 days, but K-ETA registration applies before departure. Check status closer to the date.
  • Getting around — a T-money card covers buses, metro and most taxis nationwide. Buy at any convenience store.
  • Rail — KTX for the long legs. The Korea Rail Pass only pays off if you are moving nearly every day; on this route, individual tickets are cheaper.
  • Maps — Google Maps does not do transit here. Naver Map or KakaoMap, both with English.
  • Ferries — Wando and Jeju sailings cancel in rough weather. Keep a day of slack either side of Cheongsando.
  • Cash — cards everywhere, but keep some won for island minbak and small ferries.

If 19 nights is too many

Cut Asan and Gangneung and shorten Jeju to three: 14 nights, same shape. Cut Cheongsando too and you have a conventional 12-night Korea trip — but Cheongsando is the reason to do this version.

In detail · 18 nights

Japan, properly

Tokyo, the classic middle, then west to Hiroshima and Kanazawa — the two most people skip. Ends in Fukuoka so you are not backtracking.

18nights
7stops
±€1,050return flight
±€3,400all in, per person
01

Tokyo

4 nights

Not one city but a dozen, each with its own character. Four nights is the minimum that stops it being a blur.

  • Shibuya and Shinjuku at night, then Yanaka in daylight for the old low city
  • TeamLab, booked weeks ahead — it sells out
  • A morning at Tsukiji outer market, then Ginza for the basement food halls
  • Day trip to Nikko or Kamakura if the weather is kind

Land at Haneda or Narita Haneda is closer; the Monorail then Yamanote line puts you central in 40 minutes.

02

Hakone / Mt Fuji

2 nights

Onsen country, and the only reliable way to actually see Fuji rather than the cloud where Fuji lives.

  • A ryokan with a private open-air bath — this is the night to spend money on
  • The Hakone loop: pirate ship, ropeway, and the Owakudani sulphur vents
  • Fuji is visible roughly one morning in three — plan for the disappointment

±1.5 h by Romancecar Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku, reserved seats, worth the small supplement.

03

Kyoto

4 nights

The one everyone comes for, and the one most damaged by everyone coming. Timing your days matters more here than anywhere else.

  • Fushimi Inari before 7am — genuinely empty, and completely different
  • Arashiyama bamboo at dawn, then the Sagano railway
  • Higashiyama in the evening when the day-trippers have gone
  • One day in Nara for the deer and Todai-ji

±2.5 h shinkansen Tokaido shinkansen. Sit on the right for the Fuji view if you have not already had it.

04

Osaka

2 nights

Kyoto's opposite: loud, unpretentious and built around eating. A relief after the temples.

  • Dotonbori at night, then Kuromon market in the morning
  • Okonomiyaki and kushikatsu — this is the city that does them properly
  • Osaka Castle is fine; the food is the reason

±30 min Commuter distance from Kyoto — locals treat it as one metro area.

05

Hiroshima & Miyajima

2 nights

Worth the detour west, and the pairing of the Peace Memorial with the torii at Miyajima is the emotional centre of a Japan trip.

  • The Peace Memorial Museum — give it a full morning and expect to be quiet after
  • Miyajima's floating torii at high tide, and stay overnight if you can
  • Okonomiyaki Hiroshima-style, layered rather than mixed

±1.5 h shinkansen Sanyo shinkansen. This is the leg that makes a rail pass worth pricing.

06

Kanazawa

2 nights

The Japan people miss. Kenroku-en is one of the three great gardens, and the old districts survived the war intact.

  • Kenroku-en at opening, then the samurai district of Nagamachi
  • Omicho market for crab and sea urchin
  • The 21st Century Museum, and the gold-leaf workshops

±3 h via Shin-Osaka Thruway bus or rail via the Hokuriku line.

07

Fukuoka

2 nights

The end of the line, and the ramen capital. Also the easiest place to fly home from if you do not want to backtrack.

  • Yatai food stalls along the Naka river after dark
  • Tonkotsu ramen at Ichiran's original, or better, a yatai
  • Dazaifu shrine as a half-day

Flight ±1.5 h, or shinkansen Shinkansen all the way if you have a pass; otherwise fly.

What it costs

Return flight AMS–HND±€1,050
Beds · 18 nights±€1,150
Food±€620
Rail (incl. 7-day pass)±€430
Entries & extras±€150
Per person±€3,400

Mid-range: guesthouses and business hotels, eating where locals eat.

Worth knowing

  • Visa — None needed for a Dutch passport up to 90 days. Register on Visit Japan Web to speed up arrival.
  • Rail pass — Only worth it on this route because of Hiroshima and Kanazawa. Price a 7-day pass against individual tickets before buying.
  • Booking — Cherry blossom season sells out months ahead. If you go in April, book beds before flights.
  • Golden Week — 29 April – 5 May. Trains and hotels are full and prices double. Plan around it.
  • Money — More cash than you expect. IC card (Suica) for transit and convenience stores.
  • Luggage — Use takkyubin to forward suitcases between cities — it costs about €15 and saves hauling them on the shinkansen.

If that is too long

Cut Kanazawa and Fukuoka and fly home from Osaka: 13 nights, still the full classic route. Cut Hiroshima too and it is a conventional 11-night first trip.

In detail · 19 nights

Vietnam, top to bottom

North to south, the way the country is shaped. Ha Giang early while you have energy, the Mekong at the end when you do not.

19nights
7stops
±€900return flight
±€1,900all in, per person
01

Hanoi

3 nights

Dense, loud, and the best street food in the country. The Old Quarter is chaos and that is the point.

  • Bun cha for lunch, banh mi from a cart, egg coffee at Giang
  • The Old Quarter on foot with no plan; the train street if it is still running
  • Water puppets once, for the strangeness
  • Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum and the Temple of Literature

Land at Noi Bai Grab from the airport, about 45 minutes.

02

Ha Giang Loop

4 nights

The reason to come to northern Vietnam. Limestone mountains, hairpin passes and villages that see almost no one.

  • Ride it over three to four days — Ma Pi Leng pass is the payoff
  • Hire an easy-rider driver if you are not confident on a motorbike; nobody judges
  • Homestays in Du Gia and Dong Van, dinner with the family included

±6 h by night bus Sleeper bus from Hanoi. Book the bike and driver before you arrive.

03

Ninh Binh

2 nights

Ha Long Bay's limestone karsts, but inland, among rice paddies, and reachable by bicycle.

  • Trang An by rowboat — three hours, three caves, no engine
  • Cycle to Mua Cave and climb the 500 steps at sunset
  • Bich Dong pagoda in the early morning mist

±6 h back via Hanoi Bus or train south; it is close enough to Hanoi to be a long day trip, but two nights is better.

04

Lan Ha Bay

2 nights

Ha Long without the flotilla. Same geology, a fraction of the boats.

  • An overnight on a smaller boat rather than a floating hotel
  • Kayaking into the lagoons at first light
  • Cat Ba island for the national park if you want a day on land

±2.5 h + boat Bus to Haiphong, then across. Avoid the big Ha Long day-cruise operators.

05

Hue

2 nights

The imperial capital, and the food is the most refined in the country — a different Vietnam from the north.

  • The Citadel and the Forbidden Purple City
  • Royal tombs by motorbike along the Perfume River — Tu Duc and Khai Dinh
  • Bun bo Hue where it was invented

Night train ±13 h The night train south is comfortable and saves a hotel night.

06

Hoi An

3 nights

Lantern-lit, heavily touristed, and still worth it. Also the best place in Vietnam to get clothes made.

  • The old town after the day-trippers leave, roughly 8pm
  • An Bang beach in the afternoon
  • A tailor for something fitted — allow two days for fittings
  • A cooking class, which here is genuinely good rather than a gimmick

±3 h over Hai Van Pass Hire a driver over the Hai Van Pass rather than the tunnel — the coast road is the point.

07

Ho Chi Minh City

3 nights

Faster, richer and more forward-facing than Hanoi. The war history here is unavoidable and should be.

  • The War Remnants Museum — difficult, and the reason to come
  • Cu Chi tunnels as a half-day
  • Ben Thanh and the street food around District 4
  • A Mekong Delta overnight if you have the days

Flight ±1.5 h Domestic flight from Da Nang; the train takes 17 hours.

What it costs

Return flight AMS–HAN±€900
Beds · 19 nights±€430
Food±€290
Transport incl. one flight±€200
Ha Giang bike & driver±€110
Per person±€1,930

Mid-range: guesthouses and business hotels, eating where locals eat.

Worth knowing

  • Visa — E-visa required for Dutch passports — 90 days, applied online in advance. Print the approval.
  • Ha Giang — Book the bike or easy-rider driver before arriving. Do not ride yourself unless you genuinely can.
  • Weather — The country is long enough that north and south have opposite seasons. March–April is the only month both work well.
  • Trains — The Reunification Express is comfortable in soft sleeper. Book ahead on Vietnam Railways or Baolau.
  • Money — Cash-led. Dong notes have many zeros — check what you hand over.
  • Tet — Late January to mid-February. Much of the country closes and transport is impossible. Avoid entirely.

If that is too long

Cut Hue and shorten Ha Giang to three: 14 nights. Cut Ho Chi Minh City and fly home from Da Nang for a northern-only 12 nights.

Central Asia

The Silk Road, still open.

Samarkand's turquoise tilework, Kyrgyz mountains and yurt camps, the Kazakh steppe — three countries stitched into one Silk Road run. Cheap, uncrowded, and further off the trail than anywhere else in this file.

Jordan

Petra, and everything around it.

The Siq opening onto the Treasury, a night under Wadi Rum's stars, floating in the Dead Sea at −430 m — Jordan packs an absurd amount into a small, easy-to-drive country. It made the original 2027 shortlist for a reason.

Oman

Arabia, unhurried.

Grand-mosque marble, mountain villages on Jebel Shams, a night among the Sharqiya dunes, dhows in Sur — then a flight south to Salalah, where Arabia turns green and tropical. The whole country, end to end.
